title: Reverse Odd Levels of Binary Tree
statement: `root` is the root of a **perfect** binary tree: every node that is not a leaf has exactly two children, and all leaves are at the same depth. A node's level is the number of edges between it and the root, so the root is on level 0 and its children on level 1. On every odd level (1, 3, 5, ...), reverse the order of the values: reading that level from left to right afterwards gives its old values from right to left. Values on even levels and the shape of the tree stay as they are. Return the root of the changed tree.
constraints: The tree has between 1 and 2^14 nodes
root is a perfect binary tree
notes:
## Intuition

The task is about whole levels, so a level-order (BFS) walk fits: hold one level's nodes in an array, in left-to-right order. When the array holds an odd level, reverse it by swapping values from both ends toward the middle. Only the values move; the nodes and their links stay put, so the levels below are untouched. A recursive alternative walks mirrored pairs of nodes (the left child of one with the right child of the other) and swaps their values on odd levels.

## Approach

1. Start with `level = [root]` at `depth` 0.
2. While the nodes of `level` have children (in a perfect tree, checking the first node is enough), build `next` from each node's left and right child, in order.
3. Increase `depth`. If it is odd, swap `next[i].val` with `next[j].val` while two indices `i` and `j` move inward from the ends.
4. Move on with `level = next`. When the leaves are reached, return `root`.

## Example 1, step by step

`root = [2,3,5,8,13,21,34]`. Level 0 is `[2]`. Its children form `next = [3, 5]` at depth 1, which is odd, so the two values swap: `[5, 3]`. Depth 2 is `[8, 13, 21, 34]`, even, so it stays. Those nodes are leaves, the loop ends, and the tree reads `[2,5,3,8,13,21,34]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): every node is put in a level array once and swapped at most once.
- Space: O(n): the last level of a perfect tree holds about half of the nodes.

## Pitfalls

- Swap values, not child pointers: swapping subtrees would also reorder every level below.
- Level 0 (the root) is even; the first level to reverse is the root's children.
- Stop the two indices when they meet (`i < j`); continuing past the middle swaps every pair back.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `level` | the nodes of the current level, left to right |
| `depth` | the level number of `next` once incremented |
| `next` | the children of `level`, which form the following level |
| `i`, `j` | indices moving inward from both ends of `next` |

narration.2: Begin with the root alone: level 0.
narration.3: depth counts the level being built; the root's level is 0.
narration.4: In a perfect tree, if the first node has children, every node on this level does.
narration.6: Visit the current level from left to right...
narration.7: ...and line up its children, left before right, to form the next level.
narration.9: next is one level deeper than level.
narration.11: Walk i forward from the start and j backward from the end until they meet.
narration.12: Swap the two values; the nodes and their links stay where they are.
narration.15: Move down to the level just built.
narration.17: The leaves are done; return the same root with its odd levels reversed.
